code_first.q: Trace the first midpoint decision in binary search on sorted binary place values.
code_first.code:
array weights = [1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128]
target = 32
low = 0
high = 7
mid = (low + high) DIV 2
if weights[mid] < target then
    print("Search right half")
else
    print("Check left half or match")
endif
p: Predict the midpoint index and printed decision.
Change target to 4; predict the decision.
State why binary search requires sorted data and what the value 32 represents in unsigned binary.
code_first.a: mid = (0+7) DIV 2 = 3 and weights[3] = 8; for target 32 the program prints Search right half. For target 4, it prints Check left half or match. The sorted order makes halving valid. The number 32 is the 2^5 binary place value. This models one decision; a complete search must update bounds and repeat.
